title: Coral and the Current
premise: Orsen Winterbourne, a debt-ridden storm chaser working the monsoon coast for a salvage syndicate, is hired to find a vanished government survey team. He discovers one survivor — Coral Vane, the team's cartographer, who has evidence that the syndicate's 'optimists' engineered the disappearance to bury illegal dredging data. Hunted by both the syndicate and officials who want the truth drowned, Orsen and Coral ride out the monsoon in his leaking boat, falling into something neither planned. In the end, Orsen chooses justice over repayment: he broadcasts Coral's data during the season's final storm, sacrificing his boat and freedom to the current, while Coral escapes with proof and a promise.
about_author: Cyrus Thackeray is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade documenting shipwrecks along tropical coastlines. He writes adventure novels from a houseboat whose location he refuses to disclose.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet him chasing a squall for the Meridian Salvage Syndicate, measuring life in nautical miles to outrun a debt he can never repay. A radio call interrupts: a government survey vessel has gone silent off the Sable Keys. Emotional beat: restless competence masking exhaustion — a man running on momentum alone.

chapters.title: The Optimists
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. His creditors — smiling, patient, dangerous men led by Aldous Renk — offer to forgive half his debt if he finds the missing survey gear before anyone else does. The offer feels like a gift; it reads like a trap. Emotional beat: dread dressed as opportunity, as Orsen signs on knowing better.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the survey site he finds an abandoned camp: instruments intact, lifeboat gone, no bodies, no blood. Someone erased themselves carefully. Then he finds Coral Vane hiding in a sea cave, armed and starving. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into alarm — the mystery has a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Coral
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She doesn't trust him, but her boat is gone and the monsoon is twelve hours out. She reveals fragments: the team found dredging scars where no dredging was licensed, and someone wanted the data dead. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged between two people who both know what it costs to be hunted.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They run ahead of the storm in his aging trawler, the Wren, which begins taking water faster than the bilge pump can answer. Renk's chase boat shadows them through the rain. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension — the sea closing in, trust the only dry thing aboard.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sheltering in a mangrove channel, she decrypts the team's final transmission: coordinates proving Renk's syndicate ran the illegal dredging and paid officials to vanish the survey. Orsen realizes his debt was designed to own him. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve — the trap was the whole map.

chapters.title: The Long Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Days pinned down by the monsoon. Repairs, rationed food, and the slow, unwelcome honesty of proximity. Orsen admits why he owes Renk; Coral admits she transmitted a distress call that may have doomed her team. Emotional beat: intimacy against duty — love arriving at the worst possible time.

chapters.title: Renk's Patience
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The chase boat corners them at a fuel depot. Renk offers Orsen full forgiveness for Coral and the drives. For one long minute, Orsen wants it. Emotional beat: the moral hinge — twelve years of debt measured against one person worth owing everything to.

chapters.title: The Final Storm
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. As the season's last great storm makes landfall, they run the Wren straight into it — using the chaos to reach a coastal relay tower. Under lightning and flooding decks, Orsen broadcasts the survey data wide, then stays with the sinking boat so Renk's men chase the wrong signal. Emotional beat: sacrifice as clarity — justice outside the law, paid in full.

chapters.title: After the Current
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the data breaks open an inquiry; Renk's optimists are being interviewed under less optimistic circumstances. Coral waits at a harbor town where the current runs north, watching every boat come in. One does. Emotional beat: belonging earned the hard way — love that survived the storm, and a man finally counting years instead of miles.
